Who can apply?
Students (BA, MA) from foreign universities (including scholarship programmes such as Erasmus+, Erasmus+ International Credit Mobility, DAAD, KAAD, Fulbright, Coimbra, TASSEP etc. and freemover)
As a general rule, applicants must have been enrolled at their home university for at least two semesters (Bachelor)/one semester (Master)
Applicants must stay registered as students at their home university during their exchange studies in Jena.
If you do not fall into any of these categories, please contact us at
incoming@uni-jena.de
.

Guest studies at the University Jena
Type/objective of your study visit
Select your study programme. You may apply for one, two, or three subjects which should fit to your studies at home. Choose your modules/courses from these.
Study programmes for guest students in the academic year 2024/25
pdf, 46 kb
· de
Attending subject-related courses
: Guest students should complete a Learning Agreement (“Before the Mobility”) for 30 ECTS credits before their arrival. Please read
the information on ECTS and the studies open to guest students
External link
. The study visit and individual academic achievements can only be confirmed on your Transcript of Records if you regularly attend courses throughout the semester and successfully complete the required tasks.
Guest students on research visits at a faculty of the University of Jena
: During the application process a
Supervision Agreement
pdf, 359 kb
· de
must be submitted. The research visit can only be confirmed and a Transcript of Records can only be issued if you regularly visit your research centre, actively collaborate on your project, and regularly contact your research supervisor.
Duration of your study visit
Guest students will be enrolled if they intend to stay at the University of Jena for a maximum of 12 full months. In exceptional cases, a study visit may be extended by six months upon formal request.
Semester ticket and other costs
There are
no tuition fees
at the University of Jena. Every student pays the usual
semester fee
for the semester ticket and must prove a German or European health insurance that is accepted by the University.
The usual fees are charged for extra-curricular activities (e.g. language and sports courses).
Please read our
information
on
costs and financing
your study visit.
Language skills
All modules at Bachelor's level and some modules at Master's level are taught in German. Therefore, you should acquire a sufficient level of German proficiency and demonstrate it to your home university before being nominated. The University of Jena does not request a German examination certificate, but your command of German should at least meet B2 standards (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages), so that you can follow the usual courses, complete your exercises, and communicate with teaching staff, supervisors, and other students. A few courses are held in English, for which a minimum level of B2 to C1 is required.
You can visit a
German course
at the
Language Centre
of the University to further develop your German skills.
Nomination
Applicants are nominated by their home university, on basis of the partnership agreement. The home university is asked to send
a
nomination list
xlsx, 38 kb
· de
to the International Office of the Friedrich Schiller University Jena:
incoming@uni-jena.de
or via an EWP platform
by 15 June
for winter semesters (1 October to 31 March) or the full academic year
by 15 November
for summer semesters (1 April to 30 September).
Application for guest studies
After the nomination, the International Office Jena invites students to the application portal. This usually happens at the end of May/November. Participation in the online application workshop is strongly recommended (date to be announced).
Nominated students
must apply online
by 15 July
for winter semesters (1 October to 31 March) or the full academic year
by 15 January
for summer semesters (1 April to 30 September)

research project

Admission
You can check the status of your application and notifications in the application portal. You can also download the letter of admission or exclusion there.
Accommodation
We urgently recommend that you
apply for a room in a hall of residence/student dormitory
External link
in good time. The deadlines are
15 July for the winter semester
15 January for the summer semester
When applying, please provide the exact duration of your stay in Jena. Please refer to our information about dates, semester and exam periods.
Please also see our further information on
living in Jena.
Any more questions?
You can find more information on visa, health insurance, costs, services, and many other details in our
FAQ
.
Information
If you have any questions on nominations, applications, and the admission of international guest students, please send an email to
Ms Sylvia Canario Acosta
at
